content.title: CREDENTIAL PROTECTION & ENCRYPTION
content.content:
- **Credential vault**: Connector credentials (database usernames/passwords, API keys, certificates) are encrypted at rest using org-level asymmetric RSA key pairs (AES-256 encrypted). Credentials are never stored in pipeline definitions — only referenced. Account metadata is stored in the Manager, but credential secrets (passwords) remain locally in the Ground Plex encrypted vault.

- **Enhanced Account Encryption**: Optional mode where AH retains the private RSA key. The SnapLogic control plane cannot decrypt credentials at all — only the Ground Plex nodes can decrypt them. This configuration provides full control for credential protection at the platform level.

- **Secrets manager integration**: Optional native integration with AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, and HashiCorp Vault for supported cloud-adjacent environments. Pipeline credentials are retrieved at execution time from external vaults. Pipeline credentials are retrieved at runtime from the vault without ever persisting in SnapLogic.

- **TLS 1.2+ encryption in transit**: All platform communications enforce TLS 1.2 minimum (TLS 1.3 supported). Cipher suites: AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305.

- **FQDN encryption for REST API**: All REST API requests are encrypted over HTTPS. Pipeline execution on customer-deployed Groundplexes run in customer-managed private network address space (no control-plane arbitrary filesystem access or external process intrusion outside the configured Ground Plex container).

- **Principle of least privilege**: Ground Plex runtime agents operate with minimal required OS permissions. Pipeline execution on customer-deployed Groundplexes does not commit arbitrary filesystem access or external process intrusion outside the configured Ground Plex container.
